charts.annotation: Revenue is disclosed through FY2022 and from Q1 FY2026; the gap years reported EBITDA only under the then-current segment definition.

charts.annotation: Media Solutions (FY2019-FY2020) and Matching & Solutions (FY2021 onward) are the same segment under its old and new name, shown as separate series so the FY2021 relabeling is visible rather than spliced into one line. Staffing was broken out as its own segment from FY2022.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Recruit Holdings Co., Ltd.: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Recruit Holdings Co., Ltd.: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Recruit Holdings Co., Ltd.: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Recruit Holdings Co., Ltd.: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

hrTechSegment.title: HR Technology segment
hrTechSegment.content:
HR Technology is Indeed and Glassdoor: job-ad and recruiting-software revenue, mostly pay-per-click/pay-per-application, plus the segment's own EBITDA.

For Recruit Holdings Co., Ltd.: this is the segment the market prices the group on -- it carries the US labour-market cyclicality (hiring demand drives paid clicks) that Staffing and Matching & Solutions don't share directly.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin expansion or compression as Indeed/Glassdoor integrate further
  • Revenue sensitivity to US job-opening volumes (JOLTS)
  • Segment revenue disclosure has gaps in some years; EBITDA is the more complete series

segmentEbitdaMix.title: Segment EBITDA mix
segmentEbitdaMix.content:
Recruit reports three operating segments: HR Technology (Indeed/Glassdoor), Staffing (temporary and permanent placement), and Matching & Solutions (Japan domestic media and marketing, called Media Solutions before the FY2021 segment reset).

For Recruit Holdings Co., Ltd.: HR Technology now generates the majority of group EBITDA and is the most USD/global-labour-market exposed; Staffing and Matching & Solutions are more domestically Japanese and counter-cyclical to each other historically.

What to watch:

  • Which segment is driving a consolidated EBITDA move -- the mix shifts year to year
  • Matching & Solutions/Media Solutions is one continuous business under two names; don't read the FY2021 relabeling as a step change
  • Staffing margin is structurally thinner than HR Technology's

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Recruit Holdings Co., Ltd.: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Recruit Holdings Co., Ltd.: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Recruit Holdings Co., Ltd.: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Recruit Holdings Co., Ltd.: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Recruit Holdings Co., Ltd.: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Recruit Holdings Co., Ltd.: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
